chapter_title: The Chapter of the Nazorean who questions the Teac
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation

**
¶6:**

Divine
 Truth
 in
 its judicial
 function does
 not orig
inate from evil
,
 but rather the
 operation
 of Divine Order
 itself opp
oses falsity and restra
ins evil. Yet what has
 been perceived
 is that Divine
 Truth proceeds
 forth
 to
 expose, ext
inguish, and abol
ish the
 false
 and the evil within
 the mind
.
 It
 acts
 in
 this
 manner so
 that it
 may
 render evil inoperative and arrest
 the activity
 of fals
ity within
 the interior
 person
 —
 returning
 every
 evil to the
 ruling
 love
 from
 which it originated.

**¶
11:**

Nevertheless
, the
 Divine has never
 inflicted any
 evil
 upon those
 who suffer
 spiritual cond
emnation;
 rather, they bring
 it
 upon themselves.
 It
 is the
 states produced
 by their own will and understanding that pass
 judgment
 upon them from
 within,
 and
 imm
erse them in the consuming
 fires
 of self-love and its torments
.

---


**A
 note
 on method
:** The
 phrase
 *
"lay
 it upon the head of the sinner
"* transl
ates with
 particular
 clarity
:
 *
head
* corresponds
 to the
 governing
 or
 ruling
 love
 —
 the dominant
 principle
 of
 the will
 — and therefore
 the passage
 describes
 how evil
 is
 not
 imposed
 from
 without
 but returns
 to the
 very
 love
 from
 which it proceeded
. Similarly
, *geh
enna of
 burning* res
ists
 a
 single
 neat
 substit
ution,
 but reads
 most
 faith
fully as the
 *
state
 of being
 consumed
 by one
's own cup
idities* — fire
 here
 in
 its
 inf
ernal sense,
 the
 d
evouring heat
 of self-love turned
 in
ward.
 The entire
 passage,
 in
 its spiritual sense, artic
ulates the
 Swed
enborgian principle
 that **
all
 punishment
 in
 the other
 life is not
 infl
icted by the Divine but
 flows
 from the
 evil
 itself
**,
 which
 carries
 its
 own consequence
 within
 it.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: “The judge is not a man of wickedness, but rather the work counteracts wickedness, limiting the evil. Nevertheless, what you have recounted is that the judge shall go and punish, kill and slay. He acts like this that he might annul the evil and impede the wickedness in the person; and lay it upon the head of the sinner.
“Nevertheless, God has not done anything that is ev[il to] them, rather they to themselves. It is their own deeds that shall con- demn them and cast them in the gehenna of burning.
